text:
SJS arrive at BOS on a 6-2 win at OTT, with Yaroslav Askarov making 41 saves, and sit 3-1-1 in their last five. They are without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg, and Collin Graf has taken Wennberg's spot beside Marchment and Toffoli. BOS has points in seven straight and beat SJS 6-3 on Oct 13, then shut out NSH 6-0 two days ago. The Bruins' results run ahead of their chances, though: finishing and goaltending are doing the lifting, which is the real question here.

At five on five, BOS has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) to SJS's 45%. Our model has BOS at 3.34 goals tonight and SJS at 2.88. BOS also takes 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starters Jeremy Swayman (+7.7 goals saved above expected, meaning goals prevented beyond what the shots should have allowed) and Askarov (+3.9) both have good starts. Swayman was at +26.5 last season, Askarov at -19.4.

Macklin Celebrini is 81% for a point and 43% to score, and David Pastrnak is 80% for a point. Casey Mittelstadt is one goal from 100 career goals. Our under-the-radar picks are James Hagens, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous (2.7 expected goals in his last 10 games), and JJ Peterka, at 52% for a point against a Sharks team that allows the 2nd-most expected goals per 60. Both are players to watch, not locks.
